the_rule.future_training_runs: ONE canonical seed per condition (specialists, FP generations, any new arm)
the_rule.already_collected_data: UNCHANGED and analysed as collected. D1 x3, D7 x3, D3 x2 stay multi-seed; nothing is discarded to match the new protocol retroactively.
the_rule.replication_trigger: if a single-seed result would become a scientific CLAIM, it must first be replicated at n>=2 before entering the readout

why_this_is_a_screen_not_a_confirmation.the_hazard_this_run_already_demonstrated: the two completed D7 seeds were trained under IDENTICAL conditions yet differ by .867 vs .600 on OP7 and .833 vs .933 on OP11. Same training distribution, large per-cell fingerprint variation.
why_this_is_a_screen_not_a_confirmation.consequence_at_n_equals_1: a crossover observed between two single-seed policies is NOT distinguishable from that same PPO seed noise. n=1 can find CANDIDATES; it cannot establish complementarity.
why_this_is_a_screen_not_a_confirmation.therefore: single-seed specialist probes are SCREENS. A crossover they surface is a hypothesis, and the frozen two-way-with-uncertainty crossover rule still governs whether it counts.

explicitly_prohibited: reporting a single-seed crossover as demonstrated strategic specialization
interpreting a crossover between two seeds of the SAME training condition as evidence that diversity created specialization -- that is policy variation, not strategic structure
retroactively dropping already-collected seeds to match this protocol

current_seed_counts.D3_note: seed 3700003 was killed externally at 24,576 steps (rc -1, healthy losses -- not a training failure) and marked STOPPED_BY_PROTOCOL. D3 therefore has n=2 while D1/D7 have n=3. This asymmetry is recorded, not hidden; the frozen sets artifact specifies 3 per condition.

does_not_change: the evaluation protocol (30 episodes/cell, full OP6-OP12 board)
